article.title: Why Rank-Up Rate Needs a Proper Denominator
article.why: Understand how denominator choice changes the meaning of a rank-up KPI.

paragraphs.en:
A rank-up rate seems simple: divide the number of customers who moved to a higher membership tier by the number of customers you started with. But the result can change dramatically depending on who is included in the denominator. If the denominator is not defined carefully, the KPI can look strong or weak for reasons that have little to do with the campaign.

Suppose 10,000 members are in a loyalty program and 500 move up one tier during the year. Reporting a 5 percent rank-up rate sounds reasonable. However, imagine that 4,000 members were already in the highest tier and therefore had no higher rank available. If we exclude people who could not possibly rank up, the denominator becomes 6,000 and the rate becomes 8.3 percent.

Now consider a campaign aimed only at 1,500 customers who were close to the next threshold. If 300 of them ranked up, the campaign-target rank-up rate is 20 percent. That does not contradict the 5 percent or 8.3 percent figures. Each number answers a different question.

The same issue becomes more serious when comparing groups. Treatment and control should use comparable eligible populations. If the treatment rate is calculated among customers who actually received a message, while the control rate uses all assigned customers, the comparison mixes different denominators and may be biased. Analysts should decide whether the estimand is based on assignment, eligibility, delivery, or exposure before calculating the KPI.

Time also matters. Customers need enough remaining qualification period to have a realistic chance to cross the threshold. A member who enters the analysis one week before year-end should not necessarily be treated the same as someone observed for twelve months.

A practical reporting table can therefore show several layers: all members, members eligible to rank up, customers inside the campaign target band, customers successfully contacted, and customers who actually ranked up. The main KPI should be chosen based on the business question, while the other denominators remain visible as diagnostic information.

A rank-up rate is not just a numerator divided by a convenient total. The denominator defines the population to which the statement applies. Before asking whether a rate is high or low, ask first: high or low among whom?

This principle also matters for historical comparison. If eligibility rules change from one year to the next, the same formula can produce rates that are not directly comparable. For example, expanding the program to include customers who were previously ineligible increases the denominator and can lower the rate even when the number of successful rank-ups grows. A good dashboard therefore stores the denominator definition alongside the KPI rather than treating it as invisible metadata.

For campaign evaluation, analysts may also report an intention-to-treat rate based on everyone assigned to treatment and control, because assignment preserves the experimental comparison. A secondary per-protocol or contacted-customer rate can help explain execution, but it should not silently replace the randomized denominator. Keeping these views separate prevents delivery problems from being confused with treatment effectiveness.

A useful rule is to name the denominator in the label itself. Instead of displaying only ‘Rank-Up Rate,’ use labels such as ‘Rank-Up Rate among Eligible Members’ or ‘Rank-Up Rate among Assigned Campaign Customers.’ This small design choice makes dashboards easier to audit and prevents later users from assuming a different population. When the numerator and denominator definitions travel together, the KPI becomes much harder to misuse.
paragraphs.zh:
Rank-up rate 看似只是「升級人數 ÷ 原始人數」，但 denominator 怎麼定義會讓結果大幅不同。如果母數定義不清，KPI 可能因人口範圍不同而看起來特別好或特別差，與 campaign 本身無關。

例如1萬名會員中有500人升級，可說升級率5%。但若其中4,000人已在最高 rank、不可能再升級，那 eligible denominator 其實只有6,000，升級率就變成8.3%。

若 campaign 只鎖定1,500名接近門檻的人，其中300人升級，campaign-target rank-up rate 則是20%。5%、8.3%、20%都可能同時正確，只是回答不同問題。

比較 treatment/control 時更要小心。若 treatment 用「實際收到訊息的人」當分母，control 卻用「所有被分派的人」，就混用了不同 denominator，可能造成 bias。應先決定 estimand 是基於 assignment、eligibility、delivery 還是 exposure。

時間也重要。距離資格年度結束只剩一週的人，與被觀察12個月的人，本來就不應完全等同。

實務報表可以分層呈現：全會員、可升級會員、campaign target band、成功接觸者、最終升級者。主 KPI 要跟 business question 對齊，其餘 denominator 則保留作診斷。

因此 rank-up rate 不只是 numerator 除上一個方便的總數；denominator 定義了這句話適用於哪個 population。問 rate 高不高之前，先問「是在哪一群人當中高？」

跨年比較也一樣。如果 eligibility rule 改變，即使公式相同，兩年的 rate 也可能不可直接比較。擴大資格範圍會增加 denominator，甚至在成功升級人數增加時仍讓 rate 下降，所以 dashboard 應把 denominator definition 一起保存。

Campaign evaluation 可同時報 intention-to-treat rate，因為它保留 randomized assignment；另外再報 contacted-customer rate 解釋 execution，但不能偷偷用後者取代前者。

最簡單的做法是把 denominator 寫進 KPI 名稱，例如「Rank-Up Rate among Eligible Members」。這能降低後續誤解，也讓 KPI 更容易 audit。
paragraphs.ja:
rank-up率は「昇格人数÷対象人数」のように見えますが、denominatorに誰を含めるかで意味が大きく変わります。母数定義が曖昧だと、campaignとは無関係な理由でKPIが高くも低くも見えます。

例えば1万人中500人が昇格すれば5％ですが、4千人がすでに最高rankなら、実際に昇格可能なのは6千人で、eligibleベースでは8.3％です。

さらに次thresholdに近い1,500人だけをcampaign対象とし300人が昇格したなら、target内では20％です。5％、8.3％、20％は矛盾せず、それぞれ違う問いに答えています。

treatment/control比較では、treatmentだけ「実際にmessageを受け取った人」を母数にし、controlは「割付された全員」を使うと不公平です。assignment、eligibility、delivery、exposureのどれをestimandにするかを先に決める必要があります。

残りqualification periodも重要です。年末1週間前に入った人と12か月観察された人を同じ条件で扱うとは限りません。

実務では、全会員、eligible会員、campaign target band、接触成功者、実際のrank-up者を階層で示すと分かりやすいです。main KPIはbusiness questionに合わせ、他の母数はdiagnosticとして残します。

rank-up率は単なる割り算ではなく、denominatorが「誰についての率か」を定義します。高いか低いかを聞く前に、「誰の中でか」を確認すべきです。

年度比較でもeligibility ruleが変われば同じ式でも直接比較できません。program対象を拡大すると母数が増え、昇格人数が増えてもrateが下がることがあります。denominator definitionはKPIと一緒に保存するべきです。

experimentではintention-to-treatを基本にしつつ、contacted-customer rateをexecution確認に使えます。ただしrandomized denominatorを後から別の母数へ置き換えてはいけません。

「Rank-Up Rate among Eligible Members」のようにlabel自体へ母数を書くと、dashboardの誤読を防ぎやすくなります。

vocabulary.usage: Define the denominator before calculating the rate.
Use an eligible population when appropriate.
Do not confuse assignment with exposure.
Use per-protocol as a secondary view.
Use comparable populations in treatment and control.

business.term: Before asking whether the rate is high, ask who is in the denominator.
business.explanation: 提醒團隊先確認 KPI 母數，再解讀高低。

business.term: The denominator definition should travel with the KPI.
business.explanation: 建議在 dashboard 與報告中一起保存定義。

sources: Rate construction, experimental estimands, intention-to-treat analysis, and eligibility-based KPI design.
